one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. Verified scheduled events: AT&T Q3 results before the open on Wed 2026-10-21 [34]; Verizon Q3 on Mon 2026-10-26 [33]; FOMC 2026-10-27/28 [35]; T-Mobile Q3 results and call on Wed 2026-10-28 [9]. The Dec dividend ($1.17) record date 2026-11-25 [8] falls outside the window. Dropped from round 1: the FCC 2026-10-29 '482 MHz' item, which I could not confirm at fcc.gov (403), so it carries no weight. Expectations: T-Mobile pre-guided a soft Q3 (~250K postpaid account adds vs 277K in Q2 [4], elevated churn from the July plan migration [14][15]), so the account print is largely known. FY26 EBITDA/FCF guidance was reaffirmed on 2026-09-03 [7] and is likely reaffirmed again. The swing factors are management's tone on SpaceX after the Grain deal [10] and any early 2027 color. The last earnings day was -10.75% [32], so the event alone can move the stock ~10% either way. Card-panel switching data through July (Verizon to T-Mobile 2.4x the reverse flow [18]) argues against a gross-add collapse; the peer prints on 10-21 and 10-26 will show whether the sector-wide churn is broad. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: partial reversal after a -13.27% day on a long-dated (H1 2028 [11]) competitive headline, against strongly negative momentum. Net: near-symmetric around $148.58 with a slight upward tilt (median ~$149.5) and monthly vol ~10.5%, above the 33%/3.5 = 9.4% baseline because of the earnings event.

fair_value.method: Value at 2027-10-09 (before ~$4.7 of dividends): 0.40 x P/E $157.0 (NTM EPS $14.95 x 10.5x) + 0.35 x EV/EBITDA $164.3 (6.61x company-basis LTM Core EBITDA $38.6B, less $87.6B net debt + towers, over 1,020M shares) + 0.25 x FCF yield $168.4 ($18.53/share at 11.0%) = $162.4, rounded to $162.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at 2027-10-09 $14.95 (0.25 x FY27 $14.44 + 0.75 x FY28 $15.74 = $15.41, less 3% revision haircut) x 10.5x forward P/E (8-peer median 9.95x, range 5.90x-15.46x; TMUS now 11.82x) = $157.0

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis/S&P Global next-year EPS, same non-GAAP basis as the forward P/Es of TMUS and peers. Replaces the keyed Alpha Vantage $13.94 used in round 1.

$14.44 x 1.09. Below the 17.03% 3Y consensus EPS growth [2] and FY27's +16.49% [1]: ~4-5% net income growth (EBITDA growing about with the low end of the guided ~4.5-6% service-revenue growth [6], with SpaceX D2D arriving H1 2028) plus ~4% from share count reduction.
0.25 x $14.44 + 0.75 x $15.74 = $15.41; less a 3% haircut for likely estimate cuts after the Q3 churn bump and the SpaceX overhang = $14.95.

8-peer median 9.95x (VZ, T, CMCSA, RCI, BCE, TU, AMX, VOD; CHTR excluded as distressed, DTEGY as circular). 10.5x = +5.5%, inside the range, supported by a verified 3Y EPS growth forecast of 17.03% vs 6.99% (VZ) and 11.06% (T) and network leadership (Opensignal: 12 performance awards [16]; the source does not give a total, so "of 16" was removed by the citation gate). Held below the supervisor's 11x because ~4 pts of TMUS EPS growth comes from buybacks, which a P/E should not fully reward, and the growth premium is exactly what SpaceX contests; AMX trades at 10.90x on 18.02% growth. That is 2.5% below the low end of the target.
0.25 x 37.3 + 0.75 x 39.0 = 38.575. Trailing EBITDA at the horizon, to match the trailing peer multiples (round 1 wrongly applied a trailing multiple to forward EBITDA).

Held flat to the horizon (judgment): FCF after the authorized returns is absorbed by spectrum (2027 C-band auction [14]); leverage drifts from 2.3x to ~2.2x.

1,072.7M outstanding at 2026-07-17 [5]. 2026 program $18.2B [3]; used by 2026-07-17: H1 buybacks $7.146B + H1 dividends $2.221B [5] + $0.392B buybacks Jul 1-17 [3] = $9.76B, so ~$8.44B remains. Less rest-of-2026 dividends ($1.02 x ~1,070M + $1.17 [8] x ~1,055M = ~$2.32B) leaves ~$6.1B of buybacks; at an assumed ~$160 average price that is ~38M shares. 2027: 'up to approximately $30.0 billion' of returns through 2027 [6] less the $18.2B 2026 program = ~$11.8B; less 2027 dividends ($4.68 x ~1,030M = ~$4.8B) = ~$7.0B of buybacks, ~3/4 of it ($5.3B) before 2027-10-09, ~34M shares at ~$155. Add ~5M equity-comp issuance and ~5M dilutive securities (Q2 diluted weighted 1,082.4M [4]): 1,072.7 - 38 - 34 + 10 = ~1,011M. Rounded up to 1,020M because the 2027 C-band auction [14] may crowd out buybacks; I do not credit the >$22B flexible envelope [6] for extra returns.

bear.story: SpaceX threat becomes concrete faster (quick FCC approval of the Grain 800 MHz transfer [10], a terrestrial small-cell build or an MVNO with cable [13]); plan-migration churn persists, Q4 guidance cuts the 2027 framework and consensus EPS falls ~9% to ~$14.0 NTM. TMUS de-rates to a Verizon-like ~8.2x (VZ 8.23x [22]): 8.2 x $14.0 = ~$115.

base.story: FY26 guidance is met, 2027 lands a few percent below the $40-41B EBITDA / $19.5-20.5B AFCF targets [6], buybacks take the share count toward ~1,020M, and D2D stays a 2028 story [11]. The overhang fades only partly: ~10.5x on ~$15 NTM EPS plus EV and FCF cross-checks, about my $162 fair value.

bull.story: Churn normalizes after the migration, switching data stay favorable [18], the 2027 targets are hit in full and a 2027 return program is sized above the remaining ~$11.8B [6]; Starship/V3 timing slips [13]. Re-rating to ~12.5x on ~$15.9 NTM EPS (full consensus path, FY28 +10%) = ~$200. No strategic-deal premium is included.

comps_summary.peer_range: Median over 8 peers (VZ, T, CMCSA, RCI, BCE, TU, AMX, VOD): forward P/E 5.90x-15.46x, median 9.95x; trailing EV/EBITDA 4.58x-9.72x, median 7.38x. CHTR (2.34x, distressed) and DTEGY (consolidates TMUS, circular) are listed but excluded; round-1 medians including them were 9.91x / 6.9x. All StockAnalysis at the 2026-10-09 close.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 10.5x forward P/E (+5.5% vs 9.95x); 7.75x EV/EBITDA on the peer basis (+5% vs 7.38x), applied as 6.61x on the company basis to trailing horizon EBITDA; 11.0% FCF yield vs VZ 12.44% / T 11.62%. All inside the peer range and below TMUS's own 11.82x / 8.06x today.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A small premium only, resting on verified structural gaps expected to last through Oct 2027: 3Y EPS growth forecast 17.03% vs 6.99% (VZ) and 11.06% (T) [2][22][23]; company 2027 targets still maintained [6][7]; network leadership (Opensignal [16]); and card-panel switching data showing Verizon losing 2.1-2.4 customers to T-Mobile per one coming back through July 2026, with 94.7% of switchers retained [18]. It is capped at ~5% because the growth premium is what SpaceX and cable contest, ~4 pts of EPS growth is buybacks, and AMX trades at 10.90x on 18% growth [30].

thesis_break_reason: $115 = ~8.0x the verified FY27 consensus EPS of $14.44 [1] (8.0 x 14.44 = $115.5), below Verizon's 8.23x [22], and a ~15.8% yield on the low end of the 2027 AFCF target ($19.5B / 1,072.7M = $18.18 a share [6][5]). Trading there would mean the market had abandoned both the growth premium and the 2027 framework: a cut to the $40-41B EBITDA / $19.5-20.5B AFCF targets, account adds well below the 950K-1.05M guide after the Q3 churn bump, a reversal in the switching data [18], or SpaceX securing a terrestrial or MVNO route to scale before 2028. It is ~23% below spot, about 0.8 sigma at ~30% vol, and it equals my bear case.

key_uncertainties: Whether SpaceX builds or partners for a terrestrial layer (CFO noncommittal [11]; carriers refused an MVNO per Farrar [13]; 800 MHz is a coverage rather than a capacity fix [10]). A cable partnership would be the most damaging
How long plan-migration churn stays elevated, and whether the favorable switching data through July 2026 [18] held after the 2026-07-13 price change [15]
Delivery against the 2027 targets ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF [6]); I assume a ~2.5% miss
Size of the 2027 return program: ~$11.8B left under the ~$30B framework vs a >$22B flexible envelope [6], and C-band auction cash [14]
The multiple: over 12 months this is mostly a sentiment story, since D2D service is not targeted before H1 2028 [11]
Strategic optionality (DT as controlling holder; SpaceX/TMUS speculation [19]) is unverified and kept out of every number
reasoning: Round 2 changes inputs, not the thesis. Verified facts: TMUS closed $148.58 on 2026-10-09 after a -13.27% day on SpaceX's Grain 800 MHz deal [2][10][12]; FY26 guide reaffirmed 2026-09-03 [7]; the company still maintains 2027 targets of $40-41B Core EBITDA and $19.5-20.5B AFCF [6][7]; FY27 consensus EPS is $14.44 non-GAAP [1] (I replaced the keyed, likely GAAP $13.94); net debt $84.1B plus $3.46B towers at 2.3x [4]; $18.2B 2026 return program with ~$8.4B left at 2026-07-17 (my arithmetic from [3][5]) and ~$30B of returns through 2027 [6]. Valuation: P/E $157.0 (10.5x on $14.95 NTM), EV/EBITDA $164.3 (now trailing-to-trailing on the company basis with a 2.5% haircut to the 2027 target), FCF yield $168.4; blend $162 vs $157 in round 1. Most of the lift comes from the higher EPS anchor and the 1,020M share count (vs 1,045M). Where I differ from the supervisor: I keep a 10.5x P/E (not 11x) and a 3% EPS revision haircut with FY28 +9%, because part of TMUS's EPS growth is buybacks and the premium is what SpaceX contests. Alternative-lane evidence: YipitData card-panel switching (Verizon to T-Mobile 2.4x the reverse flow in May-Jul 2026, outflow rate rising, 94.7% retention [18]) is the one alt-data series that moved a number. It is why I trim the bear probability from 0.25 to 0.22 and keep the 2027 haircut at only ~2.5%. It predates the July price change, so it does not settle the churn question. Farrar's blog (carriers refused an MVNO; next-gen constellation ~2028 [13]) supports the view that the threat reaches the P&L after the horizon. The WARN data [17] and Opensignal [16] remain context. I could not confirm the FCC 482 MHz item (fcc.gov 403), so it is removed. X/Reddit were not fetchable and no liquid prediction market on the relevant events was found, so none is used. Distribution: scenarios $115 / $160 / $200 at 0.22 / 0.53 / 0.25 (mean ~$160). The ladder is a lognormal mix: 88% with median $160 and sigma 0.27, 12% left-tail with median $118 and sigma 0.30. That gives a ladder median of ~$155 and P(>=$115) ~0.85, against a large-cap base rate of +/-25-35% and 33% realized vol. Thesis break $115. Lane note: 8 of 35 sources are in-lane. The 10 peer pages and 7 filings or company releases are required for basic facts and comps.
